trickyParts: The mirror handler must run before both deciders in the same transaction. A blocked-by-only edit is an issue.updated whose status did not change, and the engine returns early on exactly that (engine.go's `fact.Seq <= issue.LastDispatchSeq || fact.Status == issue.Status`), so neither decider could have written the row itself. internal/intake/handler_order_test.go pins the order by behaviour: a probe standing where admission stands already sees the row, and the engine alone writes none.

record.Waiting is deliberately unchanged. Dropping a blocked root from the waiting line would make record.TreeLive false for it and turn its children into orphans admitted as roots of their own; the skip lives in promoteHolds and in slotFree's count only.

A tree Legion takes back after it finished and lingered comes back at the admitted phase carrying no run, so startedRun alone did not exempt it, while a never-started child handed over from a finished tree — which the spec requires to stay checked — looks identical afterwards. The distinction exists only inside readmit (whether the tree arriving is the root's own), and the judgement happens later, so it is stored: issues.taken_back.
